products.title: Madhubani Peacock Dance Painting
products.story_en: Painted by master artist Priya Devi from Mithila, Bihar, this Madhubani masterpiece captures the eternal dance of peacocks during the monsoon. Using only natural pigments derived from turmeric, indigo, and lac on handmade paper, this 2,000-year-old tradition lives through every brushstroke.
products.story_native: मिथिला की मास्टर कलाकार प्रिया देवी द्वारा बनाई गई यह मधुबनी पेंटिंग मोरों के नृत्य को दर्शाती है।

products.title: Kanchipuram Pure Silk Saree — Temple Border
products.story_en: Woven over 10 days by master weaver Lakshmi Subramanian in Kanchipuram, Tamil Nadu, this silk saree features the iconic temple border pattern in 24-carat zari gold thread. Each thread is hand-twisted by her family in a tradition spanning five generations.
products.story_native: கரகாட்டம் கோவில் எல்லை நூல் சேலை கைத்தறியில் நெய்யப்பட்டது।

products.title: Kashmiri Walnut Wood Carved Box — Chinar Leaf Motif
products.story_en: Hand-carved from single-piece walnut grown in the Kashmir Valley, this decorative box features the chinar leaf motif that has symbolized Kashmir's cultural identity for centuries. Master craftsman Mohammad Yusuf spent 3 weeks creating this piece using traditional koftgari chiseling technique.
products.story_native: कश्मीर घाटी के अखरोट की लकड़ी से हाथ से नक्काशी किया गया यह बक्सा चिनार पत्ती के डिज़ाइन से सजाया गया है।

products.title: Jaipur Blue Pottery Vase — Floral Garden Design
products.story_en: Crafted using the rare quartz-based Jaipur blue pottery technique — not clay-based like other pottery — this vase by Sunita Prajapati features a hand-painted Persian floral garden in cobalt and turquoise. The 700-year-old craft was nearly extinct until revived by master craftswomen like Sunita.
products.story_native: जयपुर ब्लू पॉटरी की दुर्लभ क्वार्ट्ज तकनीक से बना यह फूलदान हाथ से चित्रित फारसी फूल बाग के साथ सजाया गया है।

products.title: Warli Tribal Art — Village Life Cycle Canvas
products.story_en: Painted by Warli tribal artist Mangal Singh from the foothills of the Sahyadri mountains in Maharashtra, this canvas depicts the eternal cycle of village life — harvest, dance, and community. The 3,000-year-old Warli tradition uses only white rice paste on terracotta-colored cloth, creating a living anthropological record.
products.story_native: वारली आदिवासी कलाकार मंगल सिंह द्वारा सह्याद्री पर्वत की तलहटी से बनाया गया यह कैनवास ग्राम जीवन के शाश्वत चक्र को दर्शाता है।
